# Pull Request

## Description

Completes the webhook notifications parent tracking issue by adding production observability, monitoring infrastructure, and comprehensive integration documentation for third-party webhook consumers.

### Metrics & Observability

Added 7 Prometheus metrics covering webhook delivery pipeline:
- Delivery success/failure/retry counters by event type
- Latency histograms (P95, P99) for delivery timing
- Queue size gauges (retry queue, dead-letter queue)
- Active subscriptions count
- HTTP status code distribution
- Retry attempts histogram for all delivery attempts

Metrics automatically collected during webhook delivery:

```go
// processDelivery now tracks all delivery attempts
webhookDeliveryTotal.WithLabelValues(eventType, "success").Inc()
webhookDeliveryDuration.WithLabelValues(eventType, "success").Observe(duration)
webhookHTTPStatusCode.WithLabelValues(eventType, "200").Inc()
webhookRetryAttempts.WithLabelValues(eventType, "success").Observe(float64(attemptCount))
```

### Alerting Rules

Added 9 Prometheus alerts to `monitoring/alerts.yml`:
- Failure rate alerts (warning at 10%, critical at 50%)
- Queue size alerts (retry queue, dead-letter queue)
- Latency degradation (P95 > 5s)
- No active subscriptions informational alert

### Enhanced Health Endpoint

`GET /health/webhooks` now returns comprehensive statistics:
```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "webhooks": {
    "pending_retries": 0,
    "dlq_items": 0,
    "active_subscriptions": 5,
    "pending_deliveries": 12,
    "recent_deliveries": {
      "delivered": 145,
      "failed": 2,
      "pending": 12
    }
  }
}
```

### Documentation Enhancements

Expanded `docs/backend/webhooks.md` with production integration guidance:

**Multi-language signature verification** - Added complete examples for Go, Ruby, Java, PHP (in addition to existing Node.js, Python) with proper secret management patterns demonstrating environment variable loading

**Troubleshooting section** - 20+ common issues with solutions:
- Signature verification debugging with step-by-step validation
- High failure rate root causes and mitigation
- Idempotency patterns for duplicate handling
- Local testing setup with ngrok

**Security best practices** - Production-ready patterns:
- Secret management with environment variables and secret managers
- Rate limiting implementation
- Input validation after signature verification
- Replay attack prevention
- Production security checklist (15 items)

Example security implementation:

```javascript
// Validate timestamp to prevent replay attacks
const eventTime = new Date(payload.timestamp);
const age = Date.now() - eventTime.getTime();
if (age > 5 * 60 * 1000) {
  throw new Error('Event timestamp too old');
}
```

### Review Feedback Addressed

- Updated Go and Java examples to demonstrate loading secrets from environment variables with clear fallback patterns for example purposes
- Fixed retry attempts metric to record all delivery attempts including intermediate retries for complete observability
- Removed unused signature verification failures metric (not applicable for webhook sender)
- Removed corresponding alert that referenced the unused metric
- Fixed alert runbook references to point to correct documentation sections

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Infrastructure/CI/CD change

## Testing

- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Added new tests for changes (4 test cases for webhook metrics)
- [x] Manual testing completed (backend builds successfully)

Tests verify metrics registration, counter/histogram recording, gauge updates, and label validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Comments added for complex logic
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No new warnings generated
- [x] Labels will be auto-synced from linked issues (milestone/, priority/, area/, kind/)

author: copilot
body:
## Add admin command /grollnogp to migrate {EP:GP} → {EP} with GP backup and dual-format support

### Summary
Implements admin-only migration from legacy `{EP:GP}` officer note format to `{EP}` format. Addresses Lua 5.0 runtime errors (`unexpected symbol near '#'`, `GuildRoll = nil`) reported in previous implementation attempts.

### Implementation Checklist
- [x] Add migration command `/grollnogp`
- [x] Support both {EP} and {EP:GP} formats in all EP/GP functions
- [x] Auto-convert {EP:GP} to {EP} when updating EP values
- [x] Fix pattern matching to capture all groups in init_notes_v3
- [x] Back up GP values to GuildRoll_oldGP SavedVariable
- [x] Lua 5.0 compatibility ensured

### Implementation

**Migration Function** (`GuildRoll:migrateToEPOnly`)
- Scans roster for `{EP:GP}` pattern, converts to `{EP}` preserving prefix/postfix
- Backs up GP values to `GuildRoll_oldGP` SavedVariable: `{gp, timestamp, oldNote, newNote}`
- Throttled updates via frame OnUpdate (default 0.25s, configurable, min 0.1s)
- Note length enforcement (31 char max) with proportional prefix/postfix trimming
- Roster-safe: re-lookup by name before each write to handle reordering

**Slash Commands**
- `/grollnogp [throttleDelay]` - standalone
- `/groll nogp [throttleDelay]` - via admin command table

**Dual-Format Support** (Updated Core Functions)
- `get_ep_v3`: Reads from both `{EP}` (new) and `{EP:GP}` (legacy) formats
- `get_gp_v3`: Returns GP from `{EP:GP}` or baseAE for `{EP}` format
- `init_notes_v3`: Initializes new notes in `{EP}` format, auto-converts legacy notes on ANY update
- `update_epgp_v3`: Writes in `{EP}` format, auto-converts `{EP:GP}` → `{EP}` on update
- `GuildRosterSetOfficerNote`: Detects both formats for change tracking

All addon functions (give EP, decay, reset, etc.) now work seamlessly with both formats. **Any EP update automatically converts legacy `{EP:GP}` notes to the new `{EP}` format.**

**Lua 5.0 Compatibility**
- Uses `table.getn()`, `string.len()`, `arg1` (no `#` operator)
- All API calls wrapped in `pcall` for robustness

### Example

```lua
-- Migration:
-- Before: Main{100:50}
-- After:  Main{100}

-- Reading/Writing after migration:
get_ep_v3("Player", "Main{100}") -- returns 100 ✓
update_epgp_v3(110, nil, ...) -- writes Main{110} ✓

-- Auto-conversion on update:
-- Before: {58:1}
-- Give 10 EP → writes {68} (not {10:1}) ✓

-- GP backup:
GuildRoll_oldGP["PlayerName"] = {
  gp = 50,
  timestamp = 1703030400,
  oldNote = "Main{100:50}",
  newNote = "Main{100}"
}
```

**Pattern matching**: `^(.-)({(%d+):(%-?%d+)})(.*)$` captures prefix, fullTag, ep, gp, postfix (5 groups). Supports negative GP.

**Note trimming**: When `prefix + {EP} + postfix > 31`, trims prefix/postfix proportionally: `floor((prefixLen/totalLen) * available)`.

### Files Changed
- `guildroll.lua` (+258, -50): migration function (L2093), command registration (L224, L1045), updated EP/GP functions (L1107-1726)

### Backward Compatibility
The addon now supports BOTH formats simultaneously:
- Old notes with `{EP:GP}` continue to work
- New notes with `{EP}` are fully supported
- **Any EP update auto-converts `{EP:GP}` → `{EP}`** (fixed in latest commit)
- Migration command `/grollnogp` available for bulk conversion

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed pattern matching in `init_notes_v3` to correctly capture all 5 groups (was causing legacy notes to not convert on update)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Problem: Add an admin-only migration command to convert officer notes from the legacy {EP:GP} format to the new {EP} format while backing up GP values to a SavedVariable table. Also add a slash command (/grollnogp) to trigger the migration. Ensure the implementation is robust for Turtle WoW (WoW 1.12 / Lua 5.0) and won't produce syntax errors (no use of the Lua 5.2+ length operator '#'). The repository is RollingSmile/GuildRoll and the primary file to modify is guildroll.lua (root of the addon).
> 
> Background:
> - There is an open PR that intended this feature. The user reported runtime errors: "guildrolla.lua:1744 unexpected symbol near '#'" and "GuildRoll = nil value". The migration code must avoid Lua 5.0-incompatible constructs (for example, avoid using '#' for length inside manual parsing fallbacks) and must reference GuildRoll only when it exists (guard against nil during load order).
> 
> Requirements and actionable changes:
> 1) Add a new method to GuildRoll named migrateToEPOnly (or GuildRoll:migrateToEPOnly) that:
>    - Is admin-only (checks GuildRoll:IsAdmin() and returns a friendly message if not).
>    - Scans guild roster for officer notes that contain the pattern {EP:GP} (support optional negative GP values) and converts them to {EP} while preserving surrounding prefix/postfix content.
>    - Before changing an officer note, stores a best-effort GP backup in a saved table GuildRoll_oldGP keyed by player name. Each backup entry must include gp (number), timestamp, oldNote, newNote.
>    - Avoids hard errors by wrapping API calls in pcall where appropriate (GetGuildRosterInfo, GuildRosterSetOfficerNote, GetNumGuildMembers, GetGuildInfoText, etc.).
>    - Works with roster reordering: re-lookup the member by name at time of applying the note update and use the current roster index.
>    - Throttles updates to avoid spamming the server: the function should perform note writes using a frame OnUpdate with a configurable throttleDelay (default 0.25s per change). Use CreateFrame("Frame") and SetScript("OnUpdate", ...).
>    - Ensures officer notes don't exceed MAX_NOTE_LEN (31) after conversion. If needed, trim prefix and postfix evenly to fit while preserving the EP tag.
>    - Is Lua 5.0 compatible (use string.len instead of # when the code's fallback parsing intentionally avoids '#' usage). Use table.getn rather than # where needed.
> 
> 2) Register a new admin-only chat command /grollnogp (or integrate into the existing /groll command table) that allows an admin to trigger the migration. Accepts an optional numeric throttleDelay argument (seconds) for power users, e.g. '/grollnogp 0.5'. The command should parse the argument robustly (tonumber) and call GuildRoll:migrateToEPOnly(throttleDelay). The command must be visible only to admins in the options table (if added there), and must not break existing command registration.
> 
> 3) Ensure the code is placed in guildroll.lua in an appropriate location (inside the GuildRoll scope after GuildRoll is defined but before OnEnable uses it) — suggested: add the function near other admin utilities or near migration helpers. If adding the slash command, register it in delayedInit or OnInitialize in the same file so chat commands are registered at the proper time.
> 
> 4) Defensive programming and compatibility:
>    - Use pcall for protected API calls that may fail during startup when roster isn't ready.
>    - When parsing notes, avoid Lua 5.2+ features and avoid using raw pattern replacements that can mis-handle special characters (escape them when calling string.gsub to remove a specific tag).
>    - Use string.match and string.find consistently and guard against nils.
>    - Do not change any files under Libs/
> 
> 5) Tests & verification steps to include in PR description:
>    - Reload UI (/reload) and verify no Lua syntax or runtime errors on load.
>    - As a guild officer/leader, run '/grollnogp' (and '/grollnogp 0.5') and verify:
>      * Officer notes containing {EP:GP} are converted to {EP}
>      * GuildRoll_oldGP populated with backups (check SavedVariables after logout/reload)
>      * No hard errors or spam to guild chat
>    - As non-admin, running '/grollnogp' prints a permission warning and performs no changes.

### Motivation
- Provide a triangle‑centric GNN alternative that reasons over Delaunay triangle centroids/chirality (spin‑1 local frames) alongside the existing point‑based models.
- Replace the previous chain-specific dataset API with a pair/triangle point‑cloud dataset suite suitable for parity and control tasks.
- Add a runner to easily compare multiple GNN variants under the same experimental config.
- Ensure TensorBoard logs are written to unique, timestamped subdirectories so runs do not clobber each other.

### Description
- Models: added a triangle‑based local‑frame GNN implementation in `gnn_testbed/models/triangle_lss.py` (TriangleGraphBuilder, SparseTriangleFrameLayer, TriangleLSSGNN, ChiralTriangleLSSClassifier) and exposed it via the model factory (`model.type: triangle_lss`) in `gnn_testbed/models/__init__.py` and config options (`tri_graph_mode`, `k_tri`) in `gnn_testbed/config.py`.
- Data: removed the old chain dataset and replaced it with unordered point‑cloud datasets in `gnn_testbed/data/pointcloud.py` (`PairFieldDataset`, `TriangleFieldDataset`) plus `pointcloud_collate`; updated `gnn_testbed/data/__init__.py` exports.
- Runners/configs: updated `train.py` and `run_comparison.py` to use the new datasets and config schema; added `configs/default.yaml`, `configs/comparison.yaml`, and `configs/standard_egnn.yaml` for examples; added `run_comparison.py` to train/evaluate multiple model variants and write a comparison summary.
- Training/utils: added a training module `gnn_testbed/training/trainer.py` that writes TensorBoard logs into timestamped subdirectories under `work_dir/tb/` and contains the training loop, checkpointing, and metrics logging.

### Testing
- Compiled the package and entry points to validate syntax: `python -m compileall gnn_testbed train.py run_comparison.py` — compilation succeeded.
- No full training runs were executed in CI here; the new runner and trainer are exercised only via static compilation checks in this change.
- The new models and data loaders import cleanly with the updated config schema (verified by the compile check).
- Users can run experiments with `python train.py --config configs/default.yaml` or compare models with `python run_comparison.py --config configs/comparison.yaml`.

body:
Following up from https://github.com/instantdb/instant/pull/2138, this passes along the info from our SDKs and dashboard so we can track events in Posthog.

Here's an overview of the events we'll track

| Event                  | Description                          | Sources                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `auth:complete`        | User completed OAuth login           | instant-cli, create-instant-app      |
| `app:create`           | Permanent app created                | instant-cli, dashboard, platform-sdk |
| `app:create-ephemeral` | Temporary app created (anonymous)    | create-instant-app                   |
| `app:claim`            | Ephemeral app converted to permanent | create-instant-app                   |
| `app:delete`           | App marked for deletion              | dashboard, platform-sdk              |
| `app:clear`            | App data cleared                     | dashboard                            |
| `schema:push`          | Schema deployed                      | instant-cli, dashboard, platform-sdk |
| `schema:pull`          | Schema fetched                       | instant-cli                          |
| `perms:push`           | Permissions deployed                 | instant-cli, dashboard, platform-sdk |
| `perms:pull`           | Permissions fetched                  | instant-cli                          |

For `create-instant-app` we'll also track the following which can be useful for understanding what tools are users are vibing with

| Property       | Description                                                                              |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `template`     | Base template used: `next-js-app-dir`, `vite-vanilla`, or `expo`                         |
| `aiTool`       | AI tool rules added: `cursor`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `zed`, `windsurf`, or `none` |
| `usedAiPrompt` | Whether `--ai` flag was used to generate code with Claude Code                           |


Tested events using `instant-cli`, `create-instant-app` and the dashboard and saw them all flowing into Posthog. Pretty neat!

body:
Phase 3 implements the complete pipeline for generating and evaluating trajectories from the trained diffusion model with comprehensive metrics and visualization tools.

## Sampling Module (diffusion_v7/sampling/)
- trajectory_sampler.py: TrajectoryGenerator class
  - DDIM sampling (50 steps vs 1000 DDPM steps) for fast generation
  - Classifier-free guidance (CFG) support with configurable scale
  - Batch generation with variable sequence lengths
  - Single trajectory convenience method
  - Automatic padding mask based on lengths

## Evaluation Module (diffusion_v7/evaluation/)
- metrics.py: Comprehensive evaluation metrics
  - Goal accuracy: distance error, angle error (shortest circular path)
  - Realism metrics: speed, acceleration, angular velocity distributions
  - Smoothness metric: jerk (derivative of acceleration)
  - Diversity metrics: pairwise trajectory distances per condition
  - Real vs generated comparison statistics
  - Full evaluation orchestration and formatted reporting

- visualize.py: Visualization utilities
  - Single and multi-trajectory plotting
  - Generated vs real comparison plots
  - Feature distribution histograms (all 8 trajectory features)
  - Diversity visualization (multiple samples per condition)
  - Goal accuracy scatter plots (target vs achieved)
  - Comprehensive evaluation report generator

## Generation Script (generate_diffusion_v7.py)
- Load trained checkpoints with config
- Generate trajectories from test set or random conditions
- Support for both DDIM and DDPM sampling
- Configurable CFG scale and sampling parameters
- Comprehensive evaluation with metrics and comparison to real data
- Save generated trajectories, conditions, and metadata
- Command-line interface for easy use

Usage:
  python generate_diffusion_v7.py --checkpoint checkpoints/best.pt \ --num_samples 100 \ --cfg_scale 2.0 \ --evaluate

Phase 3 Status: COMPLETE ✓
Ready for full model training and evaluation once Phase 2 training is done.

`--reuse-test (optional)pipeline-id ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Allow the new pipeline to reuse build artifacts and skip successful test stages from a specified pipeline or the last pipeline if no pipeline-id is indicated. If the Git commit ID has changed, this option will be always ignored. The DEFAULT behavior of the bot is to reuse build artifacts and successful test results from the last pipeline.

`--disable-reuse-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Explicitly prevent the pipeline from reusing build artifacts and skipping successful test stages from a previous pipeline. Ensure that all builds and tests are run regardless of previous successes.

`--disable-fail-fast ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable fail fast on build/tests/infra failures.

`--skip-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip all test stages, but still run build stages, package stages and sanity check stages. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--stage-list "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the specified test stages. Examples: "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--gpu-type "A30, H100_PCIe"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the test stages on the specified GPU types. Examples: "A30, H100_PCIe". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--test-backend "pytorch, cpp"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip test stages which don't match the specified backends. Only support [pytorch, cpp, tensorrt, triton]. Examples: "pytorch, cpp" (does not run test stages with tensorrt or triton backend). Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub pipeline status.

`--only-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--disable-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--detailed-log ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Enable flushing out all logs to the Jenkins console. This will significantly increase the log volume and may slow down the job.

author: copilot
body:
PR previews at `/SchedulingAssistant/pr/pr-{number}/` were showing blank screens because the workflow was building with the wrong base path that didn't match where the PR preview action deploys.

## Root Cause

The `rossjrw/pr-preview-action` deploys to `pr/pr-{number}/` (with "pr-" prefix), but the workflow was building with `--base="/SchedulingAssistant/pr/${PR}/"` (without the prefix). This mismatch caused all assets to be referenced at the wrong paths.

For example:
- **Actual deployment path**: `/SchedulingAssistant/pr/pr-147/`
- **Build base path**: `/SchedulingAssistant/pr/147/`
- **Result**: Assets referenced at `/SchedulingAssistant/pr/147/assets/...` but actually located at `/SchedulingAssistant/pr/pr-147/assets/...`

## Changes

- **index.html**: Extended base tag logic to detect `/repo/pr/pr-{number}/` pattern and preserve full path (all 3 segments)
- **Toolbar.tsx**: Changed hardcoded `/favicon-32x32.png` to use `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`
- **.github/workflows/pages-pr-preview.yml**: Fixed build command to use `--base="/${REPO}/pr/pr-${PR}/"` with the "pr-" prefix to match the actual deployment path

## Implementation

```javascript
// Before: Always used first segment only
base.href = '/' + pathParts[0] + '/';

// After: Detect PR preview paths with pr- prefix
if (pathParts.length >= 3 && pathParts[1] === 'pr') {
  base.href = '/' + pathParts[0] + '/' + pathParts[1] + '/' + pathParts[2] + '/';
} else {
  base.href = '/' + pathParts[0] + '/';
}
```

This preserves existing behavior for production (`/SchedulingAssistant/`) and Netlify (`/`) while fixing PR previews by matching the build base path to the actual deployment path.

author: kholyo18
body:
### Motivation
- Add Phase 2 Community features: a simple reputation system + badges, best-answer workflow for questions, a stable trending ranking, and expanded saved-post categories.
- Keep changes localized to the Community feature, maintain tag normalization, and avoid regressions in existing feed/search behavior.

### Description
- Data/model updates
  - Added `bestAnswerCommentId` and `bestAnswerAuthorId` to `PostModel` and ensured `toMap()`/`fromDoc()` include them.
  - Introduced `communityScore` usage on user documents via repository write paths (likes/comments/best answer). Score updates use Firestore transactions and `SetOptions(merge: true)` to avoid overwriting user docs.
- Reputation and trending
  - New utils: `community_score_utils.dart` implements `trendingScore(...)`, `badgeForScore(...)`, and `badgeLabel(...)` with simple thresholds (Helper >=100, Top Contributor >=500) and trending formula `likes*2 + comments*3 + freshnessBonus`.
  - Repository sorts feed by `trendingScore` when the Trending filter is active.
  - Exposed `streamCommunityScore(userId)` in `CommunityRepository` for UI badge streams.
- Best Answer
  - Added `setBestAnswer(...)` in `CommunityRepository` to set/unset `bestAnswerCommentId`/`bestAnswerAuthorId` and update comment author/community scores (+10 / -10) safely in a transaction.
  - UI: `PostDetailsScreen` pins best answer to the top and shows a localized `Best Answer` label. Post owner (OP) can mark/unmark best answers on comments.
- Saved posts categories
  - New `SavedPostCategory` enum & helpers in `saved_post_category.dart` (values: `later`, `exams`, `advice`).
  - `toggleSave()` now stores a `category` with default `later` and `updateSavedCategory()` enables editing categories.
  - Saved-post streams return categories; `CommunityScreen` shows per-saved-item category chips and allows changing category via bottom sheet; filtering by category is available when Saved filter is active.
- UI and localization
  - Updated `PostCard` and `CommentTile` to show small localized badge chips next to author names; `CommentTile` shows Best Answer badge and action for OP.
  - Community feed (`CommunityScreen`) updated to support Saved-category filters and to surface saved category editor.
  - Added ARB keys and updated generated localization files for: badge labels (`helperBadge`, `topContributorBadge`), best-answer strings (`bestAnswerLabel`, `markBestAnswer`, `unmarkBestAnswer`), saved categories (`savedCategoryLater`, `savedCategoryExams`, `savedCategoryAdvice`, `chooseCategory`, `savedToCategory`).

### Testing
- Automated tests: none executed in this rollout (no CI/test commands were run).
- Suggested smoke/manual commands for verification:
  - `flutter pub get` then `flutter run` to build and exercise the Community flows.
  - Verify like/comment interactions update `communityScore` on the author and badges update in the UI; mark/unmark best answer as OP and confirm pinned comment and score adjustments; save a post and change category, then filter by category.

This pull request introduces a new event system to the client, providing a flexible infrastructure for handling and dispatching input events such as key presses, releases, and mouse actions. The main components added are an extensible `EventBus` for event management, a set of event definitions, a registry for mapping key events to callbacks, and a comprehensive key enumeration.

**Event System Infrastructure:**

* Added the `EventBus` class (`EventBus.hpp`, `EventBus.tpp`) to handle registering event handlers, emitting events, and dispatching queued events in a thread-safe manner. This enables decoupled communication between components via events. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8319ac7de67f0e8e12347a3796af994cb379395479787492e732c9a18b919da6R1-R73) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9db898492da4161bb9e8e258cabe584a8582dd566ae2117bab78ae408ad2f255R1-R54)
* Introduced the `EventRegistry` class (`EventRegistry.hpp`, `EventRegistry.cpp`) to allow registering callback functions for specific key press and release events, leveraging the new event bus for dispatch. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9d0d74db6a8a9b49b88696a02796f25ce460430f1458e38e31a2a50a5872c76dR1-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f781e92945088c800abb7d835a1967ee424aed618c7c0e60d878166aa410ce28R1-R42)

## Summary

- Add Docker Compose configuration for running Automaker in a fully isolated container with no access to host filesystem
- Create multi-stage Dockerfiles for both UI (nginx) and server (Node.js) with security best practices (non-root user, health checks)
- Add comprehensive documentation explaining isolation benefits, usage, and security verification steps

## Problem

Automaker uses AI-powered agents that can read, write, delete files, and execute commands on the operating system. Running it directly on a user's local machine poses significant security risks, as the AI could potentially access sensitive files or cause unintended damage to the system.

## Solution

This PR introduces a Docker-based deployment option that:
- **Completely isolates** the container from the host filesystem (no volume mounts to host directories)
- Uses **named Docker volumes** for data persistence, which are container-managed
- Runs the server as a **non-root user** for additional security
- Provides a simple `docker-compose up -d` workflow for easy setup
- Documents how to optionally mount specific project directories when needed (with read-only options)

author: fercor-cisco
body:
Fixes https://github.com/googleapis/python-api-core/issues/880

## Problem:
When the retry mechanism re-raises non-retryable exceptions, it explicitly clears the exception chain by using raise final_exc from None. This breaks explicit exception chaining created with raise ... from ..., making the original cause (__cause__) inaccessible for debugging.

## Fix:
Modified `_default_exception_factory()` in `retry_base.py` to preserve the `__cause__` attribute when re-raising non-retryable exceptions. Instead of returning `(exc_list[-1], None)`, we now return `(exc_list[-1], getattr(exc_list[-1], '__cause__', None))`.

This ensures that exception chains are maintained through the retry mechanism, preserving debugging information and meeting developer expectations for exception handling.

## Testing:
Added a new test case in `tests/unit/retry/test_retry_base.py` that checks that the cause from the chained exception is preserved by `build_retry_error`.

body:
This pull request refactors the `oxdock-core` crate to depend on the `oxdock-parser` crate for all DSL parsing and AST types, and introduces a formal grammar-based parser using [`pest`]. The parser implementation and AST definitions are now centralized in `oxdock-parser`, which exposes the canonical OxDock DSL grammar for downstream tooling. The changes also update the Rust lint workflow to use nightly for Miri compatibility and add new parser dependencies.

**Parser refactor and migration:**

* All AST types (`Step`, `StepKind`, `WorkspaceTarget`, `Guard`, etc.) and parsing logic are moved from `oxdock-core` into `oxdock-parser`, which now provides a grammar-driven parser using the `pest` library. `oxdock-core` and its tests are updated to import these types and the `parse_script` function from `oxdock_parser` instead of their previous local definitions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd5d0e9ad3dd20cb7b042aba146877d0b36142eb3e9194bcdbdbbb4be68b24f6L1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9acf9c0b68a8c4e32411337832848c9ec34c477de4916cfc6ec5f9c632692e47L6-R7) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9acf9c0b68a8c4e32411337832848c9ec34c477de4916cfc6ec5f9c632692e47L174-R174) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-9acf9c0b68a8c4e32411337832848c9ec34c477de4916cfc6ec5f9c632692e47L335-R335) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-9acf9c0b68a8c4e32411337832848c9ec34c477de4916cfc6ec5f9c632692e47L588-R589) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-191a7d3f7ac5554c50e6f40c7c16f24965ad3a3b623b595efef1a1c3dd9b9b82L1-R9) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d10d51ab4b6f2fd3cc830919cd557f19af9aa707e4116e8505948da70f37ba9cL1-R3) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-d10d51ab4b6f2fd3cc830919cd557f19af9aa707e4116e8505948da70f37ba9cL306-R305) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-d10d51ab4b6f2fd3cc830919cd557f19af9aa707e4116e8505948da70f37ba9cL507-R506) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-d10d51ab4b6f2fd3cc830919cd557f19af9aa707e4116e8505948da70f37ba9cL561-R560) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-d500669e1650c5125836aa2a7c1e609fd474de406ee08995838a71d4345b211dR1-R375)

* The `oxdock-parser` crate now contains a detailed AST implementation and display logic for all supported DSL commands, guards, and step kinds, as well as quoting and formatting helpers.

**Grammar and language specification:**

* The OxDock DSL grammar is now defined in a single `.pest` file and consumed directly by the parser. The grammar is also exposed at runtime via a `LANGUAGE_SPEC` constant for use by external tools, ensuring the language definition and implementation remain in sync. The crate README is updated to document this architecture and usage.

**Dependency and feature updates:**

* Adds `pest`, `pest_derive`, and `proptest` as dependencies in `Cargo.toml` for grammar parsing and property-based testing. Updates features in `oxdock-parser` to use `proc-macro-api` instead of `token-input`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2e9d962a08321605940b5a657135052fbcef87b5e360662bb527c96d9a615542R34-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b8788c1a610597f6f543dc3397969cc6659fc69e9a6bfd50c582b1abf9e780e8L13-R26)

**Build and CI improvements:**

* Updates the Rust lint GitHub Actions workflow to use the nightly toolchain and install `rustfmt`/`clippy` for nightly, ensuring compatibility with Miri-only code paths.

**Cleanup:**

* Removes the unused `[features]` section from `oxdock-core/Cargo.toml` and cleans up module imports.

author: wlggraham
body:
## PR Details
Clickup Link - 

### Description 

The purpose of this PR is to complete the cancellation and resource cleanup process within heimdall. Currently, cancellation puts jobs in a cancelling state, which terminates the handler. This means that remote resources could still be running, however, so we want a mechanism that can pick up stale or cancelling jobs and ensure that all resources have been properly terminated. 

In order to do this, we pass the command handlers to the janitor, who then actively queries the DB for any stale or cancelling jobs. When it finds any, it grabs the appropriate cluster and activates the cleanUp Handler associated with each plugin (using the same interface that the normal handler uses). It then becomes necessary for each plugin to write a cleanup() function that will take any values from the job/command/cluster context to terminate resources. 


I have updated the ECS plugin as an example of how the above approach would be implemented. 


This PR was tested by creating multiple scripts which launched dozens of async jobs using different command criteria. The jobs would be canceled at different speeds/intervals, and the results were analyzed. 

Some things to remember: 

1. When a job is cancelled via API, the status is updated in the DB. A go routine that is monitoring that status flag runs every 10 seconds to then pass the cancellation signal to the routine running the job. This means that if the job completes (fails/succeeds) before the cancellation context is triggered, then the final status will be recorded as the final state, not canceled. This is intentional. 
2. Each Heimdall instance running will kick off a janitor every minute. It will start by creating a canceling-job channel, query any stale or canceling jobs, update the statuses, then send the jobs to a cancel channel. This means that the status' of the jobs are updated right before they are actually canceled. This is done to avoid keeping a connection open on the DB while running each plugins `cleanup()` function.

author: erseco
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to media handling and the ODE XML export structure, as well as expands supported asset types and enhances test coverage. The most important changes are grouped below by theme.

**Media Handling Improvements:**

* Added global helpers `addMediaTypes` and `simplifyMediaElements` to automatically add MIME type attributes to media elements and to convert complex MediaElement.js structures to native HTML5 video/audio elements, improving compatibility and fixing playback issues with large videos. These helpers are now called before resolving asset URLs in both `PreviewPanelManager` and `IdeviceNode`.
* Updated asset URL resolution logic to avoid converting to data URLs (using blob URLs instead), preventing memory issues with large media files.

**Asset Type and MIME Support Expansion:**

* Greatly expanded the list of supported asset file types (including more image, video, audio, document, archive, and 3D model formats) and their corresponding MIME types in `AssetManager`.

**ODE XML Export Structure Enhancements:**

* Refactored the ODE XML export logic to use a more explicit, nested structure for properties at the project, page, block, and component levels. Properties are now exported as `<odeProperty>`, `<odeNavStructureProperty>`, `<odePagStructureProperty>`, and `<odeComponentsProperty>` elements, improving clarity and extensibility. 
* The exported XML now includes additional project metadata fields and a more robust handling of block/component properties, with support for new attributes such as `iconName` and explicit page/block/component IDs. 

**Test Coverage Improvements:**

* Updated the test mocks in `ElpxExporter.test.js` to fully support and verify the new property export logic, including realistic Y.Map-like property structures for pages, blocks, and components.

author: copilot
body:
Adds support for processing Slack view submissions to create GitHub repositories via Poppit. The service now subscribes to `slack-relay-view-submission` channel, extracts form values, and publishes `gh repo create` commands.

## Changes

**Configuration**
- Added `REDIS_VIEW_SUBMISSION_CHANNEL` (default: `slack-relay-view-submission`)
- Added `REDIS_POPPIT_CHANNEL` (default: `poppit-commands`)
- Added required `GITHUB_ORG` for repository creation
- Added `WORKING_DIR` (default: `/tmp`) for Poppit execution context

**View Submission Processing**
- `handleViewSubmission()` - extracts values from nested view state (equivalent to `jq '.view.state.values | map_values(.[] | .value)'`)
- Publishes commands to Poppit in format:
```json
{
  "repo": "org/repo-name",
  "branch": "refs/heads/main",
  "type": "slash-vibe-new-repo",
  "dir": "/tmp",
  "commands": ["gh repo create org/repo-name --public --add-readme --gitignore Go --description '...'"]
}
```

**Security**
- Repository name validation (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores, dots only)
- Single-quote shell escaping for descriptions using `'\''` pattern
- Max 100 char limit on repository names

**Concurrency**
- Main loop now handles both slash command and view submission channels via select statement

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Implement new-repo command</issue_title>
> <issue_description>We will now subscribe to a redis channel (by default `slack-relay-view-submission`) and receive payloads similar to the following:
> ```

>   "view": {

>         "element": {

>         }
>       },

>         "block_id": "repo-description",
>         "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Repository Description" },
>         "element": {
>           "type": "plain_text_input",
>           "action_id": "repo_desc_input"
>         }
>       },
>       {
>         "type": "input",
>         "block_id": "ai-prompt",
>         "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Copilot Issue Prompt" },
>         "element": {
>           "type": "plain_text_input",
>           "action_id": "ai_prompt_input",
>           "multiline": true
>         }
>       }
>     ],
>     "state": {
>       "values": {
>         "repo-name": {
>           "repo_name_input": {
>             "type": "plain_text_input",
>             "value": "ExampleRepo"
>           }
>         },
>         "repo-description": {
>           "repo_desc_input": {
>             "type": "plain_text_input",
>             "value": "Description for the example repository"
>           }
>         },
>         "ai-prompt": {
>           "ai_prompt_input": {
>             "type": "plain_text_input",
>             "value": "Sample AI prompt used to create the first github issue"
>           }
>         }
>       }
>     },
>     "hash": "[REDACTED_STATE_HASH]",
>     "title": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "New Repo" },
>     "submit": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Submit" },
>     "root_view_id": "[REDACTED_VIEW_ID]",
>     "app_id": "[REDACTED_APP_ID]",
>     "app_installed_team_id": "[REDACTED_TEAM_ID]",
>     "bot_id": "[REDACTED_BOT_ID]"
>   },
>   "response_urls": [],
>   "is_enterprise_install": false
> }
> ```
> 
> We are not interested in all the fields at this stage, we are only interested in the field derived from the equivalent of the following jq query:
> ```
> jq '.view.state.values | map_values(.[] | .value)'
> ```
> eg 
> ```
> {
>   "repo-name": "ExampleRepo",
>   "repo-description": "Description for the example repository",
>   "ai-prompt": "Sample AI prompt used to create the first github issue"
> }
> ```

> ```

>   "dir": "<director>",
>   "commands": [
>     "gh repo create <org-name>/ExampleRepo --public --add-readme --gitignore Go --description \"Description for the example repository\"",
>   ]
> }
> ```
> 
> Ie will be executed by [Poppit](https://github.com/its-the-vibe/Poppit)
> 
> where the directory and org-name will be configurable via config file.
> 
> and the repo name and description are substituted from the received message payload.
> 
> For the time being ignore the `ai-prompt`, we will use it in a future enhancement.</issue_description>

author: copilot
body:
Grad-CAM visualization was leaving hooks attached and gradient tracking enabled on model parameters, causing subsequent inference calls to fail with `RuntimeError: cannot register a hook on a tensor that doesn't require gradient`. Additionally, `remove_hooks()` method compatibility varied across torchcam versions, causing `AttributeError`.

## Changes

**Enhanced hook cleanup in `visualize_activations()` (lines 2143-2162)**
- Added version-agnostic hook removal with fallback to `clear_hooks()` and `reset_hooks()`
- Explicitly disable `requires_grad` on all model parameters after Grad-CAM
- Wrapped cleanup in try-except to prevent partial failures from propagating

**Added defensive safeguard in `evaluate_image_with_statistics()` (lines 1739-1741)**
- Force `requires_grad=False` on entry to ensure clean state regardless of prior cleanup success

```python
# Before: Single cleanup method, no gradient state reset
finally:
    if cam_extractor is not None:
        cam_extractor.remove_hooks()  # May not exist in all versions

# After: Robust cleanup with gradient state restoration
finally:
    if cam_extractor is not None:
        try:
            if hasattr(cam_extractor, 'remove_hooks'):
                cam_extractor.remove_hooks()
            elif hasattr(cam_extractor, 'clear_hooks'):
                cam_extractor.clear_hooks()
            elif hasattr(cam_extractor, 'reset_hooks'):
                cam_extractor.reset_hooks()
        except Exception as e:
            st.warning(f"Aviso: Não foi possível remover hooks: {e}")
    
    # Critical: restore gradient state
    for param in model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False
```

Defense-in-depth approach ensures model returns to inference-ready state even if hook removal fails partially.

author: syedazeez337
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces comprehensive eBPF integration for real-time kernel-level monitoring of sandboxed AI agent processes. The implementation enables tracing of syscalls, file access, and network connections with minimal performance overhead.

### Key Features

- **eBPF Programs**: Three probes for syscalls (tracepoint), file access (kprobe), and network (kprobe)
- **PID Filtering**: Only traces registered sandbox processes using HashMap filters
- **Event Streaming**: Efficient RingBuf-based event delivery to userspace
- **Intent Correlation**: Links observed actions to LLM-stated intents for anomaly detection
- **Policy Configuration**: New `ebpf_monitoring` section in policy YAML

### Project Structure Changes

- Restructured to Cargo workspace with `purple/` (main crate) and `ebpf-probes/` (eBPF programs)
- eBPF programs compiled for `bpfel-unknown-none` target during build
- Feature-gated via `--features ebpf` flag

### New CLI Commands

- `monitor`: Real-time eBPF event display
- `audit`: Generate correlation reports (placeholder)
- `replay`: Session replay (placeholder)

## Test Plan

- [x] Build without eBPF feature: `cargo build`
- [x] Build with eBPF feature: `cargo build --features ebpf`
- [x] All 68 tests pass: `cargo test`
- [x] Clippy clean (only intentional dead_code warnings for future API)
- [x] Sandbox execution with eBPF: `sudo ./target/release/purple run --profile ai-dev-safe -- /bin/echo hello`
- [x] Monitor command: `sudo ./target/release/purple monitor --profile ai-dev-safe`

## Usage

```bash
# Build with eBPF support
cargo build --features ebpf --release

# Run sandbox with eBPF tracing (requires root for eBPF)
sudo ./target/release/purple run --profile ai-dev-safe -- /bin/echo "hello"

# Monitor mode
sudo ./target/release/purple monitor --profile ai-dev-safe
```

## Policy Configuration

```yaml
ebpf_monitoring:
  enabled: true
  trace_syscalls: true
  trace_files: true
  trace_network: true
  correlation_enabled: true
```

      TILE 0, 0, $10, $00
      TILE 8, 0, $11, $00
    END METASPRITE
    ```
2.  **Runtime**:
    -   `Sprite.Clear()`: Resets the internal OAM pointer (at `$19`) and clears the Shadow OAM (`$0200-$02FF`).
    -   `Sprite.Draw(x, y, metasprite)`: Draws the specified metasprite at the given global coordinates.
    -   **OAM DMA**: The generated NMI handler now automatically transfers Shadow OAM to the PPU every frame.
3.  **Compiler**:
    -   Lexer/Parser updated to handle new keywords.
    -   AST/SymbolTable updated to track Metasprites.
    -   CodeGenerator emits metasprite data tables and the necessary runtime assembly helpers.

Verified via `tests/metasprite_test.rs` which compiles a test program and inspects the resulting ROM binary for correct data structures and opcode sequences.

author: azvegint
body:
This is a test stabilization changeset for intermittent failures in the CI for Wayland. I made minimal changes where applicable. There was no goal to refactor all affected tests. * `test/jdk/java/awt/Choice/PopupPosTest/PopupPosTest.java` Without the added delay, the `stateChanged` variable could be overwritten by a previous `mouseMoveAndPressOnChoice` call. * `test/jdk/java/awt/Focus/ClearLwQueueBreakTest/ClearLwQueueBreakTest.java` The test may still fail intermittently in the CI, but an additional delay after setVisible won't cause any problems / https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8198618 * `test/jdk/java/awt/Frame/FrameSetMinimumSizeTest.java` The test made many setSize calls within a single `invokeAndWait` block and immediately checked the sizes. This works on the X11 server, but the XWayland implementation appears to be different. The `ConfigureNotify` with the correct sizes arrives later, but the test doesn't wait for it. Therefore, it was refactored. * test/jdk/java/awt/KeyboardFocusmanager/TypeAhead/ButtonActionKeyTest/ButtonActionKeyTest.java The test may still fail intermittently in the CI, but an additional delay after `setVisible` won't cause any problems / https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8257529 * `test/jdk/java/awt/LightweightComponent/LightWeightTabFocus/LightWeightTabFocus.java` mouse button was not released causing subsequent test failures. * `test/jdk/java/awt/Modal/ToFront/DialogToFrontModeless1Test.java` details are in the test's comment. This doesn't solve all the intermittent test issues related to Wayland (sometimes not even on Wayland). Some of the tests described in the bug report are no longer reproducible. I will file new issues for future failures. I also tested that it does not break other platforms testing as well. --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - [x] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8346154](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8346154): [XWayland] Some tests fail intermittently in the CI, but not locally (**Bug** - P4) ### Reviewers * [Sergey Bylokhov](https://openjdk.org/census#serb) (@mrserb - **Reviewer**) * [Phil Race](https://openjdk.org/census#prr) (@prrace - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewers without OpenJDK IDs * @khanbilal732 (no known openjdk.org user name / role) ### Reviewing

author: richardherold
body:
### Motivation
- Align the CLI with the updated spec profile vocabulary (`base`, `equipped`, `illustrated`, `lite`, `prepped`, `scalable`, `timed`).
- Avoid silently mutating recipe content when a `--profile` flag is provided while still offering a controlled override mechanism.
- Surface clear errors when a requested profile is not loaded or mismatches an existing recipe `profile` value.
- Keep output shapes from `soustack check` and existing validation flows compatible with tests.

### Description
- Updated CLI help and `supportedProfiles` in `bin/cli.ts` to the new profile names and added a `--force-profile` flag to explicitly allow overrides. 
- Added `forceProfile` to validation flags and a `resolveProfileForValidation` helper so `--profile` will set `recipe.profile` when missing and will fail with a clear `/profile` error unless `--force-profile` is provided. 
- Broadened `ProfileName` in `src/validator.ts` to include the new profiles and added a check that the requested profile schema is loaded before composing validation. 
- Updated `README.md` and `Changelog.md` to reflect the new profile vocabulary and the new CLI option.

### Testing
- Ran the full test suite with `npm test` (Jest), which builds the CLI as part of `pretest` and then runs tests. 
- All automated tests passed: `23` test suites, `475` tests, and `3` snapshots succeeded. 
- CLI-focused tests (`tests/cli.test.ts`) were executed as part of the suite and passed. 
- The build step executed during `pretest` completed successfully as part of the test run.

author: copilot
body:
Adds storage optimization features to reduce SD card usage and improve image management for the wildlife camera system.

## Changes

### Duplicate Detection
- Hash-based detection using sampled DJB2 hashing (~64 bytes across image)
- Maintains cache of 50 recent image hashes
- `saveImageWithCompression()` skips duplicates automatically

### Smart Deletion
- Quality scoring based on file size, JPEG structure validation, and content variance
- `smartDelete(targetFreeSpaceKB)` removes lowest quality images first
- Minimum 10 images always retained regardless of quality

### Compression Settings
- Configurable JPEG quality (1-63) via `setCompressionQuality()`
- Enable/disable toggle for compression and duplicate detection

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed broken `getImageFiles()`** - was completely malformed with missing variables and incomplete control flow
- **Implemented `deleteOldFiles()`** - was a placeholder, now properly removes date-based directories older than threshold

## Example Usage

```cpp
StorageManager storage;
storage.init();

// Configure features
storage.setCompressionQuality(15);
storage.setDuplicateDetectionEnabled(true);

// Save with automatic duplicate skipping
String path = storage.saveImageWithCompression(fb);
if (path.length() == 0) {
    // Either error or duplicate detected
}

// Free up space when low (target 10MB free)
int deleted = storage.smartDelete(10240);
```

## New API
- `setCompressionEnabled/Quality()`, `setDuplicateDetectionEnabled()`
- `clearDuplicateCache()`
- `smartDelete(unsigned long targetFreeSpaceKB)`
- `saveImageWithCompression(camera_fb_t*, String, bool)`
- `getStorageStats(totalImages, duplicatesSkipped, bytesCompressed)`

body:
### Motivation
- The battle embed could display stale enemy HP or skip the victory flow when player skills applied damage or DoT because embed updates ran at the wrong time.
- DoT handling and logging were inconsistent and could lead to duplicate ticks or missing log lines.
- The code must apply HP/status changes before refreshing embeds so UI reflects the correct game state.
- Ensure victory transitions happen immediately when HP hits zero.

### Description
- Reworked skill resolution flow in `game/battle_system.py` so damage/DoT application and log lines occur before any embed/room refresh.
- Fixed DoT handling to use `result.dot` consistently and emit a single log line for DoT application instead of double-applying ticks.
- Moved the `await self.update_battle_embed(...)` call to run after enemy HP/status changes (and only when victory is not triggered) so embeds are updated with fresh HP.
- Kept the out-of-battle self-buff flow unchanged but preserved status-effect persistence and ephemeral confirmations via `SessionPlayerModel` and `SessionManager` refresh.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.
- Static review of `game/battle_system.py` logic and control flow was performed while making the patch.
- Runtime verification not performed (manual execution not requested).
- Further unit/integration tests should be added to cover kill-on-skill and DoT application scenarios.

author: stefan11111
body:
Just a dump of some code I'm playing around with.
If anyone finds this useful, good for them.

This code uses [my dumb gbm backend](https://github.com/stefan11111/dumb_gbm) to create a gbm device that only creates linear gbm buffers, and tries to do egl with them.

Nvidia [doesn't allow creating `GL_TEXTURE_2D` textures with `glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES`](https://github.com/elFarto/nvidia-vaapi-driver/issues/15#issuecomment-1015827050), so I had to get creative.

The non `#if 0`-ed code maps a gbm bo and uses that map to create a texture.
The `#if 0`-ed code tells egl that our linear buffer is actually blocklinear, and creates an EGLImage from it.
Nvidia then happily creates a `GL_TEXTURE_2D` texture from it using the regular glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES` call.
The `if 0`-ed magic constant is taken from my machine and is not at all correct on other machines.
It should be queried, but I left it as is in cases anyone wants to play around with this.
The constant should be replaced with another format the card supports.

There is some other code to initially paint the buffer.

The problem with this is that it doesn't quite work.

When the gpu using this is not the primary gpu, then everything works.
We get glx working on it, and we don't care if we can actually see the contents of the buffers, only that the gpu can draw into it.

This code breaks for some reason when it's driving the primary gpu.
Nothing that is drawn appears on the screen.

I can populate the buffer for the root pixmap, which I do inside the `if 1`-ed code, and I can see what I draw there, but nothing else gets drawn.

Switching to another tty, I can see that glx is fully initialized and working, but there is no image on the screen:
```
$ DISPLAY=:1 glxinfo -B
name of display: :1
display: :1  screen: 0
direct rendering: Yes
Memory info (GL_NVX_gpu_memory_info):
    Dedicated video memory: 2048 MB
    Total available memory: 2048 MB
    Currently available dedicated video memory: 1915 MB
OpenGL vendor string: NVIDIA Corporation
OpenGL renderer string: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050/PCIe/SSE2
OpenGL core profile version string: 4.6.0 NVIDIA 470.256.02
OpenGL core profile shading language version string: 4.60 NVIDIA
OpenGL core profile context flags: (none)
OpenGL core profile profile mask: core profile

OpenGL version string: 4.6.0 NVIDIA 470.256.02
OpenGL shading language version string: 4.60 NVIDIA
OpenGL context flags: (none)
OpenGL profile mask: (none)

OpenGL ES profile version string: OpenGL ES 3.2 NVIDIA 470.256.02
OpenGL ES profile shading language version string: OpenGL ES GLSL ES 3.20
```
@ONykyf @cepelinas9000 @notbabaisyou @metux Any idea how to fix this code, or it it even can be fixed?
The point of this is to get old nvidia cards working with the modesetting driver, with full hw accel,
and without needing to use EGLStreams or vulkan.

We don't really care all that much that the gbm bo's are linear, as graphical intensive applications are usually written in vulkan, which is unaffected by this.

author: andrerfneves
body:
## Resolves #278 

## Summary

  Implements [LUD-21](https://github.com/lnurl/luds/blob/luds/21.md) which allows services to check whether a Lightning invoice has been paid by querying the LNURL server.

  **What is LUD-21?**
  When a wallet pays an LNURL invoice, the payer may want to verify that the payment was received (e.g., for proof of payment in e-commerce). LUD-21 defines a `verify` URL that returns the payment status and preimage.

  ## Changes

  ### Database Schema
  Added new table `lnurl_pay_invoices`

  ### Invoice Creation (`/lnurlp/{user}/invoice`)
  When creating an invoice, we now:
  1. Store the `res.id` from `create_lightning_invoice()` as `lightning_receive_id`
  2. Store the `res.invoice` as `bolt11_invoice`
  3. Return a `verify` URL in the response

  ### Verify Endpoint (`/lnurlp/{user}/verify?pr=lnbc...`)
  1. Parse the invoice from `pr` query param to extract `payment_hash`
  2. Look up the stored `lightning_receive_id` from the database
  3. Call `wallet.fetch_lightning_receive_payment()` to get current payment status
  4. Return LUD-21 compliant response with `settled` and `preimage`

##  Assumptions

  1. Payment is settled when preimage exists: We determine settled: true by checking if payment.payment_preimage.is_some(). This assumes Spark only populates the preimage field once the payment is fully received.
  2. Verify requires the full invoice: Per LUD-21, the verify endpoint requires the pr (invoice) as a query parameter. We parse it to extract the payment hash for lookup.
  3. Domain/username validation: We verify the invoice belongs to the user in the URL path to prevent cross-user invoice status leakage.

## Test Plan

- Create an invoice via /lnurlp/{user}/invoice?amount=10000
- Verify the response includes a verify URL
- Call verify endpoint before payment → returns {"settled": false, "preimage": null, ...}
- Pay the invoice via Lightning Network
- Call verify endpoint after payment → returns {"settled": true, "preimage": "...", ...}
- Verify that querying with an invoice from a different user returns an error
- Verify that querying with an unknown invoice returns "invoice not found"

body:
## 🧪 Unit & Integration Testing for Rating Module (Closes #35 )

### What was done
Added a comprehensive test suite for the **Rating module**, covering both **service-level business logic** and **API route behavior** to ensure rating submission.

---

## Unit Tests

Unit tests were added for the **RatingService** to validate core rating logic in isolation:

- **Rating creation rules**
  - Ensures token exists before allowing rating
  - Allows ratings **only when token status is COMPLETED**
  - Prevents duplicate ratings per token (409)
- **Rating persistence**
  - Correct association with token, branch, queue, and counter
  - Proper handling of optional comments
- **Error handling**
  - Token not found → 404
  - Invalid token state → 400
  - Duplicate rating submission → 409
- **Rating summary logic**
  - Correct aggregation of average rating
  - Accurate star-wise breakdown (1★–5★)
  - Zeroed summary returned when no ratings exist

---

## Integration Tests

Integration tests validate **end-to-end API behavior**, including routing, middleware, authorization, and database side effects:

- **Authentication enforcement**
  - All rating routes require valid JWT authentication (401)
- **Authorization enforcement**
  - `POST /ratings` restricted to CUSTOMER role
  - `GET /ratings` and `GET /ratings/summary` restricted to ADMIN / MANAGER roles
- **Rating creation flow**
  - Request payload validation
  - Successful rating submission for COMPLETED tokens (201)
  - Duplicate rating prevention (409)
- **Rating listing**
  - Paginated rating retrieval by branch
  - Correct response structure (`items`, `pagination`)
- **Rating summary**
  - Zeroed summary when no ratings exist
  - Correct aggregated summary when ratings are present
- **API responses**
  - Correct HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409)
  - Standardized response format via `ApiResponse`

---

## Routes Covered

- `POST /api/ratings`
- `GET /api/ratings`
- `GET /api/ratings/summary`


**Closes #35**

---

## 🔧 Rating Service Code Improvements

### What was improved
Refactored the **Rating service implementation** to improve **consistency, correctness, and alignment with domain models and constants**.

- [ ] Merge this PR and verify auto-merge works on subsequent PRs
- [ ] Check that Dependabot PRs can auto-merge patch/minor updates

author: dan-elliott-appneta
body:
## Summary

This PR adds Prometheus metrics support to db-up for monitoring database connection status and performance.

## Changes

- Add prometheus-client dependency (v0.19.0)
- Create MetricsConfig model with validation
- Create MetricsCollector class to expose metrics
- Update config loader to support metrics settings
- Integrate metrics into Application class
- Add 25 comprehensive tests for metrics functionality

## Metrics Exposed

All metrics include `database` and `host` labels:

1. `db_up_connection_status` (Gauge) - Current connection state (1=up, 0=down)
2. `db_up_check_duration_seconds` (Histogram) - Health check response time
3. `db_up_checks_total` (Counter) - Total checks by status
4. `db_up_errors_total` (Counter) - Errors by error code

## Configuration

Metrics are disabled by default. Enable via environment variables:

```bash
export DB_METRICS_ENABLED=true
export DB_METRICS_PORT=9090  # optional
db-up
```

Or via config file:
```yaml
metrics:
  enabled: true
  port: 9090
```

Metrics available at `http://localhost:9090/metrics`

## Test Coverage

- 25 comprehensive tests covering all metrics functionality
- Tests for MetricsConfig validation
- Tests for MetricsCollector with and without prometheus-client
- Tests for recording checks, counters, histograms, and labels
- Tests for HTTP server lifecycle and error handling

Closes #1

author: markkhl3
body:
Fixes to the following:
1) Incorrect parsing: a["FixedTimeSlots"] would return a string. Handling breaks them down from "0-1,1-2" to [["0","1"],["1","2"]] as an example. "1" is then compared with day:int. Additionally, "1" would be added to minDuration:int.

2) Each slot is currently 60 minutes wide. Addition of slot + minDuration implies that minDuration should be in terms of number of slots, e.g. 1 + 0 instead of 1 + 60 which would never be less than slot + slot_size.

3) There was an issue where tablet game (an activity that is both compulsory and recommended) would appear at a slot that is not in FixedTimeSlots.
(i) calculate_activity_availability now returns float("inf") if it finds that an activity cannot be scheduled at the current slot. Availability comparison to find most constrained should apply only to activities that can be scheduled at the current slot or later.
(ii) Added filter for compulsory activities, as handled by compulsoryScheduling using CompulsoryActivitiesOnlyView

The optimization replaces a ternary expression with an explicit if/else statement in the `iter_document_elements` method. 

**What changed**: The original code used `return (self._iter_document_elements() if self._document_contains_sections else self._iter_sectionless_document_elements())` which creates a generator expression that must be evaluated and returned. The optimized version uses direct `if/else` with `yield from` statements.

**Why it's faster**: The ternary expression creates an intermediate generator object that Python must allocate, evaluate, and then return. The direct `if/else` with `yield from` eliminates this overhead by yielding directly from the appropriate method without creating an intermediate object. This is a classic Python micro-optimization where avoiding object creation in hot paths provides measurable speedups.

body:
Integrated Distant Horizons into the Gradle build system to compile it as a separate mod JAR alongside Sodium and Iris. DH compilation will fail due to preprocessor directives (`#if MC_VER < MC_1_21_3`) but is now properly configured in the build pipeline.

## Changes

- **Version configuration**: Added `distantHorizonsVersion = '2.4.4-b-dev'` and `distantHorizonsDir = 'modules/distant-horizons'`
- **Source set**: Created `distantHorizons` source set with paths to `common/src/main/java` and `fabric/src/main/java`
- **Dependencies**: Configured compilation dependencies on Fabric Loader and Minecraft (main) outputs
- **Build tasks**: 
  - `processDistantHorizonsResources`: Substitutes version and metadata in `fabric.mod.json`
  - `distantHorizonsJar`: Assembles mod JAR to `build/mods/`
- **Task dependencies**: Added `distantHorizonsJar` to `runClient` and `clientDist` tasks
- **Toggle property**: Added `distanthorizons` property to `gradle.properties` (defaults to `true`)
  - When `distanthorizons=true`: All DH source sets, configurations, and tasks are created; DH is compiled and included in builds
  - When `distanthorizons=false`: All DH-related configuration is skipped; build behaves as it did before DH was added
  - Can be toggled by editing `gradle.properties` or via command line: `gradle runClient -Pdistanthorizons=false`

Pattern mirrors existing Sodium and Iris integration. The `runClient` task now depends on DH compilation and will fail until preprocessor issues are resolved. DH can be easily disabled by setting the property to `false`.

💡 What: Removed `last_known_fx_rates.copy()` in the daily backdating loop in `custom_components/pp_reader/backdating/holdings.py`.
🎯 Why: Creating a copy of the dictionary for every single day in the backdating range (which can be thousands of days) is expensive and creates unnecessary garbage. Since the dictionary is treated as read-only by the consumers within the loop iteration, the copy is redundant.
📊 Impact: Reduces memory allocation and copying overhead in the main calculation loop.
🔬 Measurement: Verified via simulated benchmark that avoiding copy is ~40% faster for this specific loop structure. Existing tests confirm correctness.

body:
Implements missing ProDOS file I/O commands and Apple II PEEK/POKE/CALL address compatibility from features.md (~95% of outstanding features).

## ProDOS File Operations

**Commands:** OPEN, CLOSE, APPEND, FLUSH, CREATE, LOCK, UNLOCK, POSITION, BLOAD, BSAVE, BRUN

```basic
10 CREATE "data.bin"
20 BSAVE "data.bin",A2048,L100
30 BLOAD "data.bin",A2048
40 DELETE "data.bin"
```

- Added `FileManager` singleton for handle management and file I/O state
- Commands support both immediate mode and program statements
- Binary file operations handle address/length parameters

## Apple II Memory Address Support

**Extended PEEK/POKE for 50+ special addresses:**
- Keyboard input (-16384/49152) and strobe (49168)
- Button inputs (49249-49251)
- Display control (32-37, 49232-49239)
- Annunciator outputs (49240-49247)
- Graphics memory pointers (103-104, 16384, 24576)
- Shape table pointers (232-233)

```basic
10 POKE 232,0: POKE 233,32  ' Set shape table pointer
20 POKE 49240,0             ' Annunciator 0 off
30 X = PEEK(49152)          ' Read keyboard
```

Negative addresses convert to 16-bit unsigned for Apple II convention.

## CALL Address Implementation

**12 ROM routines:** -936 (HOME), -868 (CLREOL), -3086 (clear hi-res), -151 (monitor), 768 (user ML), 1002 (ProDOS), others

```basic
10 CALL -936  ' Clear screen and home cursor
20 CALL -868  ' Clear to end of line
```

ROM calls either execute ANSI equivalents or stub with descriptive output.

## Implementation Details

- Token types added for new commands in `TokenType` enum
- Statement classes follow existing pattern (`OpenFileStmt`, `BloadFileStmt`, etc.)
- Memory functions handle special addresses before range checking
- Parser handles complex parameter formats (A#, L#, R#, B# notation)
- All 58 existing tests pass; 6 new test files added

## Remaining Items

- ProDOS RESTORE/STORE for variables (distinct from array STORE)
- Shape table binary file loading (DATA-based already supported)
- ProDOS error codes 2-21

## Summary

Wire all primary Architect dashboard reads through `teamLoader.getTeam(worldId)` for world-aware data loading. When a world is selected, data flows through the fallback chain: world snapshot → parent world → base team.

### Changes

**New utility: `src/features/architect/utils/worldTeamData.ts`**
- `loadWorldTeamData(worldId, teamId)` - centralizes world-aware team loading
- Uses `teamLoader.getTeam()` when worldId is set, falls back to base loading when null

**Updated data loading in `useArchitectState.ts`**
- Effect 5 now uses `loadWorldTeamData(worldId, teamId)` 
- `worldId` added as dependency - changing worlds reloads data
- Legacy plan loading only triggers when no world is selected

**Updated Trade Machine (`useTradeMachine.js`)**
- Added `worldId` parameter to hook signature
- Secondary teams load with world awareness via `loadWorldTeamData`

**Component wiring**
- `GMDashboard` → `TradeSection` → `TradeEditor` → `useTradeMachine` now passes `worldId`

### Example flow
```typescript
// World-aware loading (worldId set)
const data = await loadWorldTeamData('world-abc', 'lakers');
// → teamLoader.getTeam('world-abc', 'LAL') 
// → fallback chain: world snapshot → parent → base

// Base-only loading (worldId null)  
const data = await loadWorldTeamData(null, 'lakers');
// → loadTeamCapSheet('lakers')
```

### Documentation
- Updated `ARCHITECT_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`: Phase 2B complete, overall 85% → 90%

author: mccartyp
body:
### Motivation
- Provide users with visible TLS certificate metadata in the REST server preferences so they can verify issuer and expiry information without leaving the app.
- Surface certificate expiry state and warn when a certificate is expired or approaching expiration.
- Use the configured certificate (or the default generated path) to extract metadata when HTTPS is enabled.

### Description
- Added UI elements `labelTlsCertificateIcon` and `labelTlsCertificateStatus` in `dlgprefrestserverdlg.ui` to show certificate metadata and a warning icon.
- Implemented `updateTlsCertificateStatus()` in `dlgprefrestserver.cpp` which reads the certificate via `QSslCertificate::fromPath`, formats issuer and expiry, and toggles the warning icon when expired or within `kCertificateExpiryWarningDays` days; it is wired to `lineEditCertPath` changes and called from `updateTlsState()` and `updateStatusLabels()`.
- Exposed `RestServerSettings::defaultCertificatePath()` in `restserversettings.h/cpp` so the preferences dialog can fall back to the default certificate path when no explicit path is set.
- Added necessary includes (`QSslCertificate`, `QFileInfo`, `QLocale`, `QDir`) and a configurable expiry threshold constant `kCertificateExpiryWarningDays`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: copilot
body:
Performance audit identified several inefficiencies: N sequential git processes, redundant fs.stat calls, and always-on snowfall animations.

## Changes

### `scripts/gen-meta.js` — O(N) → O(1) git commands
- Replace per-file `git log` calls with single `git log --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR`
- Use Set for O(1) file lookups when parsing output
- Conditional path normalization (Windows only)

```javascript
// Before: N git processes
files.forEach((file) => {
  execSync(`git log -1 --format=%cs "${relativePath}"`);
});

// After: 1 git process
const gitOutput = execSync("git log --format=%cs --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR");
const fileSet = new Set(files.map(f => normalizePath(path.relative(rootDir, f))));
```

### `app/sitemap.ts` — Reduced fs syscalls
- Use `readdirSync({ withFileTypes: true })` to avoid stat calls on directories
- Only stat MDX/MD files that need mtime
- Eliminate duplicate path construction for layout file

### `components/last-updated.tsx` — Avoid array allocation
- Replace array creation + `.find()` with direct property lookups via short-circuit evaluation

### `components/snowfall.tsx` — Accessibility & performance
- Add `prefers-reduced-motion` support via `useSyncExternalStore`
- Skip animation rendering entirely when reduced motion is preferred
- Add SSR safety guards

author: meredecade
body: **Feature (Content Authoring)** This PR addresses the bug/feature described in issue #12002 ## Acknowledgement - [x] I acknowledge that I have read and understand the [Contributing](https://github.com/endless-sky/endless-sky/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) article. ## Summary - Mission actions can have a `to trigger` node to add conditions that, *if false*, will prevent the action from triggering. - A single mission triggers can now have multiple actions associated with it by defining duplicate `on ` nodes. - When duplicates are present, actions are run, in order[^1], until one of the actions passes the `to trigger` check (this is the blocking action) - An action can be defined as `non-blocking`[^2][^3], which means it will never prevent future actions from running - In an effort to keep the ever-increasing scope of this PR in-check, this PR does *not* include any changes to timers [^1]: Minor exception for `on enter` triggers: system specific `on enter` triggers always run before generic `on enter` trigger, regardless of the order in the data file. [^2]: `on offer` cannot be `non-blocking` (otherwise it's possible to accept/decline the same mission multiple times, which is a rat's nest of both logic and code bugs.) [^3]: I'm using `non-blocking` (rather than `blocking`) for backwards compatability. Without this PR, `on enter` has its system-specific trigger block the generic trigger. ## Usage examples Displaying a different dialog when killing an NPC, based on your reputation: ``` npc on kill to trigger "reputation: Republic" >= 0 dialog `Hunting carriers won't exactly improve your standing with the navy.` on kill to trigger "reputation: Republic" >= -1000 dialog `Each carrier you kill is just digging you in deeper.` on kill to trigger "reputation: Republic" < -1000 dialog `You're making great progress towards "public enemy number one."` [...] ``` Giving different completion messages based on credits: ``` mission on complete to trigger "credits" < 10 dialog `Mission complete, with barely any money in the bank.` on complete dialog `Mission complete.` [...] ``` Accumulating multiple conditions into a single "piracy chance" (which can be used for npc spawns, branching, etc.) ``` mission on accept non-blocking "piracy chance" ++ on accept non-blocking to trigger "credits" > 1000000 "piracy chance" ++ on accept non-blocking to trigger has "told stranger about treasure map" "piracy chance" ++ ``` ## Testing Done - [x] Used plugin to verify most/all mission and NPC actions (blocking and non-blocking). - [x] Minimal negative test using existing game data. - [x] Regression test (escort jobs, FW campaign, etc.) - [x] Minimal performance testing (fairly large fight seemed to perform ok, same for a few dozen NPCs each with `on kill` triggers) - [x] Measure before/after numbers for various performance tests ## Save File This plugin adds a bunch of jobs that can test various scenarios: [pr-12015-plugin.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24463738/pr-12015-plugin.zip) This save file was used for perfomances tests: [PR 12015~Perf.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24463746/PR.12015.Perf.txt) ## Wiki Update [Wiki PR](https://github.com/endless-sky/endless-sky-wiki/pull/204) ## Performance Impact Using the attached save, profiled a big fight both with and without this PR. After several trials, observed that peak CPU seems very similar/within margin of error: Master: PR: That said, I did observe an anomaly where master had a few frames of low CPU right after launch, before it then jumped to peak usage, whereas the PR did not. (I don't know if that means anything.)

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
The issue was that Tutors were creating excursions that were not assigned to any cycle or class, and they could not see relevant excursions in their dashboard. This happened because the application relied on the `user` object from `useAuth` (persisted in `localStorage`) which contained stale data (missing `classId` if it was assigned after login).

I fixed this by modifying `ExcursionManager.tsx` and `Dashboard.tsx` to always fetch the latest user data from the synchronized mock database (`db`) using the user's ID. This ensures that the current `classId` is used for creating excursions and filtering the dashboard view.

Changes:
- `src/components/ExcursionManager.tsx`: Added `currentUser` resolution and updated `handleCreateNew`, `loadData`, `handleDuplicateToClass`, and scope change logic to use `currentUser.classId`.
- `src/components/Dashboard.tsx`: Added `currentUser` resolution and updated `relevantExcursions` filter to use `currentUser.classId`.
- Installed `typescript` dev dependency to fix build.

## **User description** ## Summary Implements comprehensive support for Claude Code slash commands with all new features from the official documentation. ## New Features ### 1. File Referencing with `@` - Reference files directly in command prompts: `@filepath` - Use with arguments: `@$1`, `@$2` - Example: `Compare @src/old.js with @src/new.js` ### 2. Bash Execution with `!` - Execute bash commands inline: `` !`command` `` - Requires `Bash` in `allowed-tools` - Example: `` Current status: !`git status` `` ### 3. Argument Handling - `$ARGUMENTS` - All arguments passed to command - `$1`, `$2`, `$3`...`$9` - Individual positional arguments - `argument-hint` frontmatter field for documentation ### 4. Namespacing - Organize commands in subdirectories - `.claude/commands/git/status.md` → `/git.status` ## Changes ### Updated Documentation - **`.claude/skills/creating-claude-commands/SKILL.md`** - Added comprehensive documentation for all new features - Multiple real-world examples - Best practices and patterns ### New Tool - **`.claude/commands/create-slash-command.md`** - Slash command for generating slash commands - Includes templates, validation, and examples - Use: `/create-slash-command [description]` ### Comprehensive Testing - **28 integration tests** (all passing) - Tests for file referencing (`@` syntax) - Tests for bash execution (`!` syntax) - Tests for argument handling - Tests for frontmatter parsing - Tests for round-trip conversions - Tests for edge cases ## Test Coverage ```bash ✓ 28 tests passing ✓ Basic slash command features (3) ✓ File referencing with @ (3) ✓ Bash execution with ! (4) ✓ Argument handling (4) ✓ Combined features (3) ✓ Frontmatter field variations (3) ✓ Edge cases (5) ✓ Conversion quality (2) ``` ## Documentation Reference Based on: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Add Claude slash command support: file references, inline bash, argument placeholders, namespacing, generator, and integration tests ### What Changed - Commands can reference files with @ (e.g., @src/file.js and @$1) and those references are preserved through parsing and round-trip conversion - Inline bash execution using !`...` is recognized and preserved; Bash tool permissions (e.g., Bash(git *)) are extracted from frontmatter - Argument placeholders ($ARGUMENTS, $1–$9) and argument-hint frontmatter are parsed, preserved, and round-tripped - Namespacing via subdirectories is documented (commands in .claude/commands/subdir/name.md map to /subdir.name) - Adds a /create-slash-command generator template and extensive documentation updates with examples and best practices - Introduces 28 integration tests covering file refs, bash execution, argument handling, frontmatter variations, round-trip conversion, and edge cases ### Impact `✅ Clearer slash command templates for authors` `✅ Shorter command authoring with generator and examples` `✅ Fewer round-trip conversion regressions in command content`
